leyEgreso.title: State's Children Law
leyEgreso.subtitle: Law 2479 of 2025 - A step toward autonomy for youth in protection
leyEgreso.queEs: What is the State's Children Law
leyEgreso.queEsDesc: Law 2479 of 2025, known as the "State's Children Law", was approved by the Colombian Congress on July 15, 2025 and creates the National Comprehensive Support Program for graduates of the ICBF protection system. This law aims to guarantee comprehensive support, social inclusion and real opportunities for young people leaving the ICBF who lack family or community support networks. It was driven by ASCEP since 2019, initially championed by congressman Jhon Arley Murillo and taken up in 2023 by Senator Lorena Rios.
leyEgreso.obj1: Strengthen state services for young graduates
leyEgreso.obj2: Establish support networks with social and community organizations
leyEgreso.obj3: Facilitate social inclusion and access to job and educational opportunities
leyEgreso.obj4: Develop social, emotional, educational and job skills
leyEgreso.obj5: Provide economic support during the transition
leyEgreso.est1Desc: Creation of Support Units with interdisciplinary teams. Personalized support in life project, health, employment and autonomy.
leyEgreso.est2Desc: Monthly subsidy for 6 months after graduation, through the DPS.
leyEgreso.est3Desc: Basic, secondary and higher education (ICETEX, SENA). Formal employment and entrepreneurship with incentives. Loans and subsidies with preferential rates.
leyEgreso.est4Desc: Participation of CSOs, private sector, religious organizations and volunteers.
leyEgreso.est5Desc: Commitment signing and possibility of monitoring the program.
leyEgreso.dir1: Young people between 18 and 28 who lived under ICBF protection measures
leyEgreso.dir2: Youth about to graduate without family networks or support
leyEgreso.dir3: People with disabilities under ICBF protection who need permanent support
leyEgreso.dirExtra1Desc: Teams responsible for care and preparation for autonomous life of adolescents under protection.
leyEgreso.dirExtra2Desc: Entities interested in youth employability, education, mental health, housing, entrepreneurship, spirituality, culture and support networks.
leyEgreso.cambioDesc: The law creates the National Comprehensive Support Program, providing health, education, subsidies and psychosocial support. It includes Comprehensive Support Units to strengthen skills and economic support equivalent to 80% of the minimum wage for six months after leaving the system. It also promotes autonomy and comprehensive well-being through employment programs, business training and preferential credit lines.
leyEgreso.implementacionDesc: Law 2479 of 2025 assigns the Colombian Institute of Family Welfare (ICBF) a central and operational role in implementing its objectives. The ICBF, as head of the National Family Welfare System, has several key responsibilities:
leyEgreso.impl1: Formulate, coordinate and implement the National Comprehensive Support Program within 24 months of the law taking effect.
leyEgreso.impl2: Create and strengthen Graduate Support Units, made up of interdisciplinary teams.
leyEgreso.impl3: Incorporate the national registry of graduates.
leyEgreso.alcanceDesc: Law 2479 of 2025 has national reach: it applies in all 32 departments of Colombia and regulates the National Comprehensive Support Program under ICBF coordination. From its headquarters in Cali, Valle del Cauca, ASCEP works with graduate networks, social organizations and institutions across the country so the law reaches every young person leaving the protection system.
leyEgreso.papelEgresadosDesc: Graduates of the protection system should not only be beneficiaries of Law 2479, but active subjects, co-responsible and protagonists of its implementation, monitoring and improvement. The law exists because organized graduates raised their voices; therefore, their natural role is to guard its meaning, monitor compliance and bring it to life in the territories.
leyEgreso.pe4: Social leaders and agents of change
leyEgreso.papelASCEPDesc: ASCEP is the organization called to sustain the meaning, implementation and social sustainability of Law 2479. It was not only its promoter: today it is its main social reference actor.
leyEgreso.pa1: Promoter and guardian of the spirit of the law
leyEgreso.pa3: Social and political oversight of implementation
leyEgreso.pa5: Generator of knowledge and good practices
leyEgreso.procesoDesc: The bill was driven by graduates themselves through ASCEP, backed by Senator Lorena Rios and with reports by Alexandra Vasquez and Jairo Cristo. It was approved in the Congress of the Republic and signed by President Gustavo Petro.
leyEgreso.participaDesc: Effective implementation requires commitment from everyone: government, civil society, private sector and media. You can raise awareness in your community, volunteer as a mentor, establish partnerships with ASCEP and ICBF, and advocate for public policies that guarantee the well-being of young graduates.

egresadoPost.title: Graduation
egresadoPost.subtitle: We celebrate those who took the most important step: building their life project outside the protection system, with autonomy and dignity.
egresadoPost.queEsDesc: Graduation Day celebrates a milestone: the moment a young person who grew up under the state protection system transitions to independent adult life. For ASCEP, each graduation is a collective victory that deserves to be recognized, celebrated, and shared with the whole community.
egresadoPost.proceso: Graduating is not an event, it is a process
egresadoPost.procesoDesc: Behind every graduation there are years of accompaniment, training, and the building of support networks. That is why we celebrate it not as an endpoint, but as the beginning of a stage of autonomy, rights, and opportunities.

casasPost.title: Casas del
casasPost.subtitle: An integral accompaniment model for young people in the process of leaving the state protection system to build their transition to independent adult life.
casasPost.queEs: What are the Casas del Saber
casasPost.queEsDesc: The Casas del Saber are ASCEP's program that comprehensively accompanies young people in the process of leaving and those who have left the ICBF state protection system. Through a pedagogical, housing, and self-sustaining model, the program articulates five intervention areas with four thematic training lines, strengthening autonomy, emotional well-being, and leadership capacity to build solid, sustainable, and meaningful life projects.
casasPost.proposito: We transform life projects through a pedagogical, housing, and self-sustaining model, aimed at strengthening the capacities of young people with lived experience in the state protection system.
casasPost.modalidadesDesc: The program offers two ways to participate, depending on each young person's situation.
casasPost.modalidad1Desc: For young people without a support network or stable housing conditions. They access a shared physical house (maximum 8 people per home) as a safe, pedagogical, and community space, with stays of up to 24 months and progressive, planned graduation.
casasPost.modalidad2Desc: For young people with basic housing conditions already solved who need accompaniment in their graduation process. Includes psychosocial, socio-educational, and labor insertion support and thematic training.
casasPost.areasDesc: The program's operational base is organized into five areas that accompany all young people, residents and non-residents alike.
casasPost.area1Desc: Guarantees the material conditions for daily life and well-being.
casasPost.area2Desc: Continuous psychological and social support, cross-cutting to all lines.
casasPost.area3Desc: Training and development of life skills.
casasPost.area4Desc: Preparation for the labor market and entrepreneurship.
casasPost.area5Desc: Articulation of resources and inter-institutional advocacy.
casasPost.lineasDesc: Communities of practice where young people learn by doing, build collective projects, and develop skills for life and work in specific sectors.
casasPost.linea1Desc: Train community researchers capable of reading, documenting, and transforming their social environment.
casasPost.linea2Desc: Develop technological creativity and innovation aimed at solving real problems with social impact.
casasPost.linea3Desc: Foster identity, artistic expression, and the development of creative projects with cultural and economic value.
casasPost.linea4Desc: Promote emotional well-being, the life project, and community leadership as axes of social transformation.
casasPost.rutaDesc: The transition to adult life is organized into three progressive phases, with follow-up after graduation.
casasPost.fase1Desc: Initial psychosocial assessment, construction of the individual itinerary, joining the thematic line, document regularization, and short-term goal setting.
casasPost.fase2Desc: Active development in the thematic line, training in the Independent Life School, internships, network strengthening, and building the productive project.
casasPost.fase3Desc: Personalized graduation plan, consolidation of the labor project or entrepreneurship, progressive transfer of responsibilities, and post-graduation follow-up at 3, 6, and 12 months.
casasPost.estructuraDesc: The model relies on a clear structure: houses for up to 8 young people, lines with up to 12 participants, thematic leaders, a psychosocial team, a network of tutors and mentors, and general coordination responsible for inter-institutional articulation.
casasPost.datoClave: A young person in the process of leaving needs comprehensive accompaniment to build their life project with autonomy. The Casas del Saber articulate housing, training, psychosocial support, and labor insertion in a single model.
casasPost.galeriaDesc: A look at the program's daily life: training, art, technology, and community.
casasPost.ctaDesc: Explore the pedagogical, housing, and self-sustaining model that transforms life projects.

resolucion4775.title: Guideline for the Transformation of Care and
resolucion4775.slogan: Deinstitutionalizing is guaranteeing the right to live in family and in community.
resolucion4775.datoClave: Resolution 4775 of 2026 gives the ICBF a roadmap to progressively reduce institutionalization and move toward care in family and community settings.
resolucion4775.queEsDesc: The Guideline for the Transformation of Care and Deinstitutionalization is an institutional instrument for planning, coordination, technical guidance and monitoring of the ICBF. Its purpose is to prevent unnecessary, prolonged or structural institutionalization; promote the progressive transition from institutional services to family- and community-based services; and foster intersystem coordination to ensure the sustainability of deinstitutionalization.
resolucion4775.obj1: Prevent unnecessary, prolonged or structural institutionalization
resolucion4775.obj2: Promote the transition toward family- and community-based services
resolucion4775.obj3: Strengthen family and community care alternatives
resolucion4775.obj4: Ensure the sustainability of deinstitutionalization and prevent reinstitutionalization
resolucion4775.definicionesDesc: The Resolution adopts three definitions that guide the entire care transformation policy.
resolucion4775.def1Desc: A continuous, progressive process to reduce and overcome the structural, prolonged or unnecessary use of institutionalization, guaranteeing the right to live independently and be included in the community.
resolucion4775.def2Desc: A care approach where people live or remain in settings that, due to their organization and practices, generate isolation, segregation or unjustified restriction of the exercise of rights.
resolucion4775.def3Desc: Practices that seek to homogenize and exercise disproportionate control during care, limiting decision-making, participation and performance in natural settings.
resolucion4775.linea1: Prevention of family separation and institutionalization
resolucion4775.linea2: Transformation of the protection system toward models that favor life in family and community
resolucion4775.linea3: Promotion and participation to build inclusive and deinstitutionalizing cultures
resolucion4775.linea4: Intersystem coordination for the sustainability of deinstitutionalization and social inclusion
resolucion4775.estableceDesc: The Resolution defines the actions to implement the Guideline progressively and with monitoring across the ICBF.
resolucion4775.est1Desc: The General Subdirectorate will create, within 30 days, a national technical committee for care transformation and deinstitutionalization, linked to the Differential Rights Approach Model (MEDD).
resolucion4775.est2Desc: The actions will be incorporated into the national and regional annual action plan of the MEDD, with defined goals, responsible parties and deliverables.
resolucion4775.est3Desc: The General Subdirectorate, with support from the Planning and Management Control Directorate, will monitor implementation every four months.
resolucion4775.participacionDesc: The implementation of the Guideline must guarantee effective and inclusive participation mechanisms for children, adolescents, young people, families, care leavers, social organizations and actors of the National Family Welfare System (SNBF), during socialization, follow-up and adjustment phases.
resolucion4775.ascep: What does it mean for ASCEP?
resolucion4775.ascepDesc: Deinstitutionalization is the horizon of ASCEP's work: leaving the protection system is not an event, it is a process. This Guideline strengthens the path toward family- and community-based care models and validates the advocacy we have driven for years to transform the alternative care system.
resolucion4775.ctaDesc: Learn how to participate in building inclusive and deinstitutionalizing cultures in Colombia.

modelo.dim1Desc: Positive valuation of oneself and one's own history.
modelo.dim2Desc: Ability to establish quality social relationships based on trust.
modelo.dim3Desc: Perception of control over one's environment and ability to create favorable surroundings.

modelo.dim5Desc: Ability to have clear goals and define vital objectives.
modelo.dim6Desc: Development of individual potential to grow as a person.

quienesSomos.heroSubtitle: We are people who grew up under the care of the State —in ICBF foster homes— and who, upon coming of age, leave the protection system to face adult life without a family to support us. From that experience, we have come together to transform the way the State cares for and protects children and adolescents in Colombia.
quienesSomos.historiaP1: Between 2015 and 2017, three young graduates of the Colombian State protection system —Jhon Eduar Angulo, Maicol Londoño and Henrry Quiñones— turned their experience into a cause. They decided to found an initiative to support those who, like them, faced alone the transition from institutionalization to adult life, a critical and neglected stage.
quienesSomos.historiaP2: Their purpose: that no graduate of the system should have to face life without support. From empathy and lived experience, they denounced the State's lack of preparation and the absence of networks that would allow them to fully integrate into society. Their work seeks to build paths of autonomy, dignity and opportunity for a historically excluded population.
quienesSomos.historiaP3: We are an organization that has overcome the learning curve and is now in a stage of growth, strengthening its advocacy across different programmatic lines. Our leadership has made us a reference nationally and across Latin America.
quienesSomos.historiaP4: This has led us to be invited to different advocacy and decision-making spaces that contribute to transforming care systems for children, adolescents and young people with lived experience in institutional care.
quienesSomos.historiaP5: We are a new voice for the transformation of care systems in Colombia and for accompanying adolescents and young people in their transition to an autonomous and independent life.
quienesSomos.misionDesc: To develop and strengthen capacities that enhance the individual and ease the transition of adolescents and young people from the protection system toward an autonomous, dignified and full life, promoting their integral development and effective access to labor, educational, mental health and housing opportunities, while advocating for public policies, institutional practices and community dynamics that guarantee the exercise of their rights, strengthen support networks and family capacities, and contribute to preventing the loss of parental care.
quienesSomos.visionDesc: By 2030, to establish ourselves as a key articulating actor in Colombia for the transformation of alternative care models, promoting family-based practices and progressive autonomy for young people, and advocating for public policies that ensure dignified exits from the protection system.
quienesSomos.propositoCardDesc: We promote the autonomy and leadership of adolescents and young people with experience in State protection, recognizing them as rights holders and protagonists of change. Through family intervention and comprehensive accompaniment models, we foster their social inclusion and lead reforms to the alternative care system.
quienesSomos.comoDesc: Our vision comes to life through three actions: we connect young people with key actors in the protection system, facilitate spaces and tools that strengthen their capacities, and drive the transformation of alternative care in Colombia and the region.
quienesSomos.conectarDesc: We connect our beneficiaries with key actors within the protection system so the voices of pre-graduates and graduates are heard.
quienesSomos.facilitarDesc: We facilitate spaces and tools that enable pre-graduates and graduates to strengthen their skills, and operators to innovate in their care model.
quienesSomos.impulsarDesc: We drive the transformation of the protection system in Colombia and Latin America through sociopolitical advocacy and research.
quienesSomos.objetivoDesc: To promote strategies that comprehensively improve the quality of life of adolescents and young people in transition or graduates of the protection system, fostering their autonomy, empowerment, access to rights and active participation in society.
quienesSomos.oe1Desc: Strengthen the leadership, advocacy and collective organization capacities of young people with experience in the care system. Promote youth networks at local, regional and national levels as platforms for action, support and mobilization.
quienesSomos.oe2Desc: Promote structural reforms in the alternative care system to improve exit processes. Defend rights through advocacy actions, resource mobilization and free legal counsel. Promote the recognition of graduates as a group with specific rights and differentiated needs.
quienesSomos.oe3Desc: Support the development of programs and public policies based on good practices, centered on the well-being of graduates. Propose standards for independent living and support services that guarantee a dignified and sustainable transition, including vocational training and job placement.
quienesSomos.oe4Desc: Monitor the impact of programs developed by and for graduates. Generate technical and empirical evidence to guide public policy and international cooperation decisions. Continuously evaluate and adapt institutional actions to ensure impact and relevance.
quienesSomos.equipoDesc: We are a group of people who graduated from the State Protection System who, from our own experience, work to transform how the State approaches the care of adolescents and youth in Colombia.
quienesSomos.enfoqueDesc: Our model focuses on strengthening the self as the foundation for young people leaving the protection system to manage their life project. We work transversally on the six dimensions of Carol Ryff's psychological well-being across all our processes.
quienesSomos.dimensionDesc1: Positive appraisal of oneself and one's own history.
quienesSomos.dimensionDesc2: Ability to establish and maintain quality, trusting social relationships.
quienesSomos.dimensionDesc3: Perception of control over one's environment and the ability to create favorable surroundings.
quienesSomos.dimensionDesc4: Ability to sustain one's own individuality and personal self-determination.
quienesSomos.dimensionDesc5: Ability to have clear goals and define vital objectives.
quienesSomos.dimensionDesc6: Development of individual potential to grow as a person.
quienesSomos.areasTrabajoDesc: Our methodology recognizes that young people are protagonists of their life project. All our activities and trainings respond to their interests and needs, ensuring meaningful impact.
quienesSomos.areaADesc: We focus on the person. We promote active listening and mediation, access to tools that strengthen autonomy, and three key pillars: a reference figure, a space and something to do.
quienesSomos.areaBDesc: We foster insertion into non-formal and formal education. We offer vocational accompaniment, educational guidance during and after the transition to autonomy, and management of scholarships and agreements.
quienesSomos.areaCDesc: We promote access to health and training in sexual and reproductive rights. We provide counseling, guidance on State programs and psychological support.
quienesSomos.areaDDesc: We believe in employment as an engine of change. We offer training in job skills, access to vocational experiences in companies, and management of internships and job placement.
quienesSomos.areaEDesc: We amplify the voice of young people in advocacy spaces. We promote leadership training, exchange of experiences between graduates and decision makers, and participation in reforms.
quienesSomos.areaFDesc: We recognize that each young person has their own pace. We avoid unnecessary pressure, provide accompaniment according to their life trajectory and adapt to social and economic changes.
quienesSomos.poblacionDesc: Adolescents and young people between 14 and 28 years old, under State protection or already graduated, in basic or higher education processes, who require accompaniment and support in building capacities and strengthening life skills, psychosocial skills, and job preparation and connection.
quienesSomos.ctaDesc: If you share our vision, we invite you to join as an ally, volunteer or donor.

quienesSomos.ley2479Desc: Since 2019, together with political actors, we have promoted a bill to guarantee real conditions for young people leaving protection. In 2025, Law 2479 was approved, creating the Comprehensive Support Program for ICBF Graduates: strengthening the state offer and consolidating support networks for those leaving the care of ICBF.
quienesSomos.trayectoriaLead: Tap each year to see the milestones that built the path toward Law 2479 of 2025.

items: Contribution to the creation of the Latin American Network of Protection Graduates.
Formal constitution of the organization: the start of a steady, rigorous, well-done process.
First place at the Cívico Award for a Better City in Social Innovation.
1st Forum on Protection Graduation in Colombia.
Youth Leaders Summit in Brussels, European Parliament — “No one left behind”.
High-impact political forum at the United Nations, New York.
“Joining forces to end the institutionalization of children and adolescents in Latin America and the Caribbean”, Panama.
IV Congress of the Latin American Network of Protection Graduates — Road to Autonomy, Mexico.
2nd Forum on Protection Graduation: “Let us know their stories”.
Filing of the bill that years later would give rise to Law 2479.
3rd Forum on Protection Graduation: “The future of the children of the State”.
Meeting of the Care Leaders Council, Nairobi.
Debate of the bill in the ad hoc committee on childhood and adolescence.
Development and implementation of the “Voices that inspire” campaign.
Memorandum of understanding with ICBF to strengthen capacities and life projects of adolescents and young people.
Participation in the ad hoc committee to formalize an interinstitutional alliance on childhood and adolescence.
Approval of Law 2479 “Children of the State”: it creates the Comprehensive Support Program for ICBF Graduates.
Participation in the launch of the global children's campaign letter, within the framework of the United Nations Assembly.

quienesSomos.valor1Text: We believe in the value and ability of our founding members and team, our greatest asset. Teamwork is the key force to reach our goals.
quienesSomos.valor2Text: We build relationships based on two-way trust, dialogue and respect, essential for living with the diversity of beneficiaries, allies and donors.
quienesSomos.valor3Text: We fulfill our obligations with efficiency, discipline and solidarity. We believe in equal opportunity regardless of gender, ethnicity, beliefs or social position.
quienesSomos.valor4Text: We defend people's right to exercise their freedom within the law, keeping a balance between rights and responsibilities.
